sources.excerpt: Admitted for worsening shortness of breath and swelling in both legs.
1. Acute decompensated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. 2. Community-acquired pneumonia, improving.
Chronic kidney disease stage 3; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; chronic venous insufficiency.

Jordan Sample was treated during this fictional admission with intravenous diuresis and antibiotics. Oxygen was weaned before discharge. Kidney function was monitored while fluid status improved. The inpatient cardiology team reviewed the echocardiogram, and physical therapy assessed safe mobility. This paragraph describes the hospital stay; it is not a new instruction for home.
Procedures: Transthoracic echocardiogram on March 3, 2031.
Consultations: Cardiology; Physical Therapy; Care Management.
Disposition: Home with visiting nurse services. Code status: Full code. Allergies: Penicillin - rash (as written in this fictional record).
START furosemide 40 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily for 7 days.
CONTINUE carvedilol 12.5 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily.
CHANGE lisinopril 10 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily. HOLD if systolic blood pressure is < 100 mmHg.
STOP ibuprofen 200 mg tablet: Do not resume unless your prescriber gives new instructions.
TEMPORARY doxycycline 100 mg capsule: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 3 days, then stop.
CONTINUE insulin glargine 100 units/mL: Inject 8 units under the skin nightly.
CONTINUE atorvastatin 20 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet by mouth nightly.
HOLD metformin 500 mg tablet until the kidney-function recheck is reviewed; ask the prescribing clinician when to resume.
CHANGE potassium chloride 10 mEq tablet: Take 2 tablets (20 mEq) by mouth
once daily for 5 days, then resume 10 mEq once daily.
Weigh yourself every morning after using the bathroom and before breakfast. Call the cardiology office the same day if your weight increases by > 2 lb in 24 hours or > 5 lb in 7 days.
Have a basic metabolic panel checked within 48 hours. The ordering clinic will review potassium and kidney-function results.
Schedule cardiology follow-up within 5-7 days. Schedule primary care follow-up within 7 days. Pulmonary clinic follow-up is requested in 2-4 weeks.
Limit sodium to 2,000 mg per day. Limit total fluids to 1.5 L per day until the cardiology visit.
Use the rolling walker for all walking until Physical Therapy says it is no longer needed. Do not lift more than 10 lb for 7 days.
Visiting nurse: first home visit within 48 hours for medication reconciliation and symptom review.
Pending at discharge: final blood culture report and basic metabolic panel recheck. Ask the primary care office to confirm that results were reviewed.
Call the care team now for new or worsening shortness of breath, new chest pressure, fainting, confusion, inability to keep medicines down, or swelling that is rapidly worsening.
The document instructs you to call the cardiology office the same day for the weight thresholds listed on page 3. If you believe you are experiencing an emergency, contact local emergency services.
Review the Heart Failure Zone Scale attached to these instructions. The referenced scale was not included in this synthetic packet.
Bring this medication list and your morning weight log to each follow-up visit.
Medication action list states: continue insulin glargine 10 units under the skin nightly.

Diuresis: removal of extra fluid through increased urination. Ejection fraction: a measure of how much blood the heart pumps with each beat. Basic metabolic panel: a blood test that includes kidney-function and electrolyte measurements.

warnings: Hospital-course narrative is background context, not a home action.
Final medication item continues on page 3.
